.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 247 PM EDT Thursday...

1. Scattered showers continue at times tonight into Friday, 
before drier and cooler air arrives on Friday night into Saturday. 

2. Several rounds of rainfall expected through the first half 
of next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 247 PM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: GOES-19 mid level water vapor imagery shows deep
dry layer acrs our cwa, which has help to limit the areal 
coverage of showers this aftn. A weak impulse is approaching the
Ottawa Valley with a pocket of better mid lvl moisture and 
instability and should be near the SLV by 22z this evening. This
wl quickly move eastward acrs the Dacks, before falling apart 
in the CPV by midnight tonight. Have highest pops over the 
SLV/Northern Dacks this evening. Additional s/w energy is 
located north of Lake Huron and wl swing acrs our cwa on Friday 
with more scattered showers expected, especially favorable 
upslope areas of the Dacks and northern/central Greens. 
Soundings indicate lingering instability overnight, combined 
with upslope flow under llvl caa, should keep clouds persisting 
in the mtns, even after sunset this evening. These clouds and 
winds wl keep temps in the mid 30s to mid 40s. 

For Friday, still thinking a few wet snow flakes are possible above 
3500 feet, especially as progged 850mb temps drop below 0C per 
latest RAP13 data by 12z. Highest probability of precip wl be acrs 
the northern/central Greens and into parts of the CPV on Friday 
morning. Once again very steep lapse rates are anticipated on Friday 
aftn with summit temps in the mid/upper 30s, while valleys warm into 
the upper 50s to lower 60s. Favorable mixing should help to advect 
drier air aloft toward the sfc with dwpts falling back into the 30s 
and lower 40s again on Friday aftn with breezy west/northwest winds 
15 to 30 mph. 

By 12z Saturday 1032mb high pres is progged to be centered over 
northern NY, but  925mb to 850mb winds are still 15 to 30 knots from 
the northwest and some 850 to 500mb moisture is already approaching 
the area associated with waa. Have bumped temps upwards slightly 
from my thoughts yesterday, but still thinking mid/upper 20s SLK to 
upper 30s/lower 40s near Lake Champlain. Plenty of sunshine and 
comfortable temps are expected on Saturday with highs mid 50s to 
lower 60s. As sfc high pres shifts toward the Gulf of Maine, 
southerly gradient develops on Sat night into Sunday with moderate 
waa. Progged 925mb temps warm btwn 10-12C by 12z Sunday with 
increasing 925mb to 850mb winds of 20 to 35 knots. Progged soundings 
indicate a sharp and shallow llvl inversion developing Sat night, 
support a wide range temps from cooler valleys to warmer 
midslopes/summits with highs back into the 60s on Sunday.

KEY MESSAGE 2: The forecast is quite challenging late Sunday into 
Monday as the exact track of Hurricane Isaias will determine how wet 
the end of the weekend and early next week. The global deterministic 
guidance continues to show the remnants of Isaias bringing rainfall 
the region Sunday night and Monday morning while the ensemble 
guidance remains a bit split. A strong Bermuda high pressure system 
over the western Atlantic is expected to suppress how far east the 
remnants can initially track. A strengthening mid-level jet is 
expected to develop on the southern side of the remnants as the 
hurricane becomes extratropical which should push any precipitation 
associated with the remnants quickly across the region with no 
significant impact with rainfall amounts likely less than half of an 
inch. An upper level trough will likely continue in the wake of the 
remnants with a building ridge of high pressure expected across the 
central US. This will put Vermont and northern New York under 
northwesterly flow aloft with the potential for one or two cold 
fronts through the middle of next week with chances for rainfall 
associated with each of these fronts. Again, no significant 
rainfall is expected. The pattern overall is wet and messy, but 
isn't expected to be impactful.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z THURSDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Through 18Z Friday...Shower activity has been a bit more
widespread than initially forecast but the impacts have been
very minor. With plenty of drier air in the low levels, we have
seen some light rain and many terminals but no decrease in
visibility. This trend will continue through 00Z with scattered
showers briefly impacting terminals with no impact to flight
categories. Winds will remain gusty out of the west this
afternoon with gusts up to 25-30 knots at times. Some of the
showers have produced stronger gusts in excess of 30 knots but
these increases have been very short-lived. Winds will drop
below 10 knots after 00Z with light westerly winds continuing
overnight. Winds will once again become gusty after 12Z on
Friday in the 15 to 20 knot range at all terminals. VFR ceilings
and visibilities will continue through the TAF period.

Outlook...

Friday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday Night: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Columbus Day: Mainly MVFR, with areas IFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Monday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Tuesday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Likely SHRA.
